newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM aluminium futures rise in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM aluminium futures rise in dull trade.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished higher in thin trade on Friday, with the dollar's rebound failing to lure more players into the market ahead of the weekend, traders said.
"It was very quiet," said a trader. "We saw the yen falling (against the dollar) but the market failed to react seriously."
The benchmark June contract, which was launched on Thursday, ended up 1.8 yen at 187.1 yen, while others ranged from unchanged to 1.5 yen higher.
Estimated volume remained a thin 1,019 lots.
The dollar's recovery to above 114 yen during Asian trading hours from close to 113 yen early in the morning came on top of a stable finish in aluminium overnight in London.
Three-month aluminium on the London Metal Exchange (LME) added $8 to $1,577 per tonne on Thursday, helped by falling stocks and forward consumer interest.
